claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Human–AI interaction is a field of research and a sub-field of human–computer interaction, focusing on user experience and psychological factors.
claims.quote: **Human–AI interaction**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human%E2%80%93AI_interaction#cite_note-1) is a field of research and a sub-field of [human–computer interaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human%E2%80%93computer_interaction "Human–computer interaction"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human%E2%80%93AI_interaction#cite_note-:16-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human%E2%80%93AI_interaction#cite_note-3) focusing on [user experience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_experience_design "User experience design") and psychological factors.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human%E2%80%93AI_interaction#cite_note-:18-4)

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: AI is described as tools designed to mechanize tasks requiring human intelligence and replicate abilities such as navigating uncertainty, active learning, and processing information in different contexts.
claims.quote: [Artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence "Artificial intelligence") has fluid definitions and varied research applications,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human%E2%80%93AI_interaction#cite_note-:14-8) but in brief can be applied to mechanizing tasks that would require human intelligence to complete.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human%E2%80%93AI_interaction#cite_note-:15-9) AI are tools designed to replicate the human abilities of navigating uncertainty, active learning, and processing information in different contexts.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human%E2%80%93AI_interaction#cite_note-:15-9)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human%E2%80%93AI_interaction#cite_note-:14-8)

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Within HCI and HAX research, AI is divided into two subfields: natural language processing and computer vision.
claims.quote: Within the context of HCI and HAX research, artificial intelligence can be broken into two sub-fields, [natural language processing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_language_processing "Natural language processing") (NLP) and [computer vision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_vision "Computer vision") (CV).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human%E2%80%93AI_interaction#cite_note-:17-10)

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: Human–AI interaction is characterized by a more collaborative relationship between the AI and human user, unlike human-computer interaction where a human directs a machine; AI is perceived as an active agent rather than a tool.
claims.quote: As a new and rapidly developing technology,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human%E2%80%93AI_interaction#cite_note-:18-4)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human%E2%80%93AI_interaction#cite_note-:13-11) unlike human-computer interaction, where a human directs a machine, human-AI interaction is characterized by a more collaborative relationship between the computer program (the AI) and the human user,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human%E2%80%93AI_interaction#cite_note-:13-11) as AI is perceived as an active agent rather than a tool.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human%E2%80%93AI_interaction#cite_note-:16-2)

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: The changing dynamic of human–AI interaction creates new questions and necessitates new research methods not present in traditional HCI research.
claims.quote: This changing dynamic creates new questions and necessitates new research methods that are not present in traditional HCI research.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human%E2%80%93AI_interaction#cite_note-:16-2)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human%E2%80%93AI_interaction#cite_note-:18-4)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human%E2%80%93AI_interaction#cite_note-:19-7)

claims.question: q1
claims.claim: AI technologies notably include machine learning, deep learning, neural networks, and large language models.
claims.quote: AI technologies notably include [machine-learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_learning "Machine learning"), [deep-learning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_learning "Deep learning") and [neural networks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_network_(machine_learning) "Neural network (machine learning)"), and [large-language models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_language_model "Large language model") (LLMs).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human%E2%80%93AI_interaction#cite_note-:17-10)
